title: Caps, spikes and bad answers
desc: Trace a spike to its source, decide pooled versus per-user, and use feedback and terminations.
learningGoal: After this lesson the learner can react to an 80%-of-cap warning with a decision instead of a guess, and can tell a cost problem from a quality problem.

steps.title: The email, the cap and the wall at 100%
steps.bodyMd:
Marieke is the organisation admin at Van Dijk Groep, a sixty-person Dutch SME. One Tuesday she gets a mail: **"Bee Flow: 80% of your monthly cost limit reached"**.

Three things are worth knowing before anyone touches a setting:

- The warning is sent **once per billing period**, to at most **five** administrator addresses — so no second mail arrives when you pass 90%.
- The **cap** is the organisation's monthly AI ceiling. Below it nothing changes.
- At **100%** AI calls are **blocked** until the next period. The chat refuses with a message naming the amount and telling the user to contact their administrator. Reporting screens keep working — only the AI calls stop.

So the mail is a warning, not a failure. You have room to look before you act.

steps.title: The period is not the month, the range is not the gauge
steps.bodyMd:
Two windows are easy to mix up.

The **billing period** follows the subscription's billing cycle start, not the calendar month. If Van Dijk Groep's cycle starts on the 6th, usage resets on the 6th.

On **Settings → Organisation → Usage & Monitoring**, the bar **AI usage vs. cap** is drawn against that billing period: green under 80%, amber from 80%, red from 95%.

The **RANGE** control at the top right (Today, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, All, Custom — 30d when you open the page) changes every list *underneath* the gauge. It never moves the gauge. Set the range to 7d and the gauge still shows the whole period.

steps.title: This is the report
steps.body: Usage & Monitoring, with the range control on its right and the tabs Overview, Feedback and Terminations below. Nothing here changes a setting — it is a read-only report.

steps.title: The report shows, License & Usage decides
steps.bodyMd:
Nothing on Usage & Monitoring changes behaviour. The two controls that do sit at the top of the same Organisation group, on **Settings → Organisation → License & Usage**:

- the **plan card**, with the plan limits — users, agents and knowledge sources — and the **monthly cost cap** with its own percentage-used figure;
- the section **AI usage sharing**, with the toggle **Share AI usage across the organisation** and the caption **Pooled across the organisation** or **Each user has their own budget**.

That section only appears when the organisation has a subscription with a real cost budget. Both changes are reversible — the toggle can go back the same afternoon, and the gauge simply re-reads the new cap.

steps.title: Triage the spike in the right order
steps.instruction: Van Dijk Groep's gauge shows 86%. Put the admin's five moves in the order that produces a decision instead of a guess.

items.label: Read the gauge: how far into the billing period are we, and how deep into the cap?
Click the heaviest row in Top users by cost, so the All Users pill becomes that person's name
Read By tier: which model tier the spend went on
Read By app area to see which part of the product made the calls
Decide: change the plan, split the budget, or fix the routine that is spending

sim.feedback: Start with the gauge: 86% halfway through a period is a different problem from 86% on the last day. Then narrow — who, on what tier, from which part of the product. A tier is the speed-versus-depth choice behind a model: Fast is cheap, Deep Thinking is not. Clicking a row filters every panel to that person; the All Users pill brings the organisation back.

steps.title: The one-line shortcut: cost · 30d
steps.bodyMd:
Marieke does not always need the report to know who the heavy users are. On **Settings → Organisation → Users & Groups**, every row under **Organisation Members** carries an amount on the right with the caption **cost · 30d**. Hover it and the tooltip spells the figure out: *"{calls} requests · {cost} (last 30 days)"* — for Sanne in sales, something like *1,284 requests · $41.9032 (last 30 days)*.

Two cautions. The window is a rolling **last 30 days**: it is not the billing period the gauge measures, and the RANGE control on Usage & Monitoring does not move it. And the amount is only drawn for members with recorded spend, on wider screens — a row without it is a colleague who has spent nothing, not a figure that failed to load.

steps.title: Which screen answers it fastest?
steps.instruction: Four questions Marieke asks in one afternoon at Van Dijk Groep. Pair each one with the screen that answers it with the least work.

pairs.left: Who is spending the most, and I want the answer in ten seconds
pairs.right: The cost · 30d amount on the member rows in Users & Groups
pairs.note: The member list already carries each person's AI spend, so you can spot the heaviest user without opening a report at all.

pairs.left: Was that spend one enormous job, or thousands of small ones?
pairs.note: The tooltip adds the request count next to the amount — a few costly calls and a flood of cheap ones need different fixes.

pairs.left: How much of this billing period's cap is already gone?
pairs.right: The AI usage vs. cap bar on Usage & Monitoring
pairs.note: cost · 30d is a rolling 30 days. Only the gauge is drawn against the billing period, which is the window the block at 100% follows.

pairs.left: Which model tier did that person's budget go on?
pairs.right: By tier on the Overview tab, with her row clicked in Top users by cost
pairs.note: Clicking the row filters every panel to that person, so By tier then shows her spend rather than the organisation's.

steps.question: Van Dijk Groep switches Share AI usage across the organisation off. What actually changes?

choices.label: The same cap is divided into per-seat slices, so the heaviest user is blocked first instead of draining the shared pool.
The monthly bill goes down, because each user now costs less.
choices.feedback: The cap is unchanged — only the way it is divided changes. Nothing about per-call cost moves, so the bill is exactly what the usage says it is.

choices.label: The 80% warning email stops firing until every user is over their own slice.
choices.feedback: The organisation-wide warning still fires off the pooled total, so the admin keeps seeing plan-wide pressure whichever mode is on.

choices.label: The gauge resets to zero for the rest of the period.
choices.feedback: The gauge reads usage already recorded in this billing period. It only resets when the next period starts.

steps.explanation: Per-user mode gives each active seat the cap divided by the number of active seats. It is a fairness control, not a cost control: the total the organisation can spend is the same, but one heavy user can no longer take everyone else's room, and that user hits a personal block message instead of the whole team hitting the organisation-wide one.

steps.title: Feedback: complaints with the model attached
steps.bodyMd:
"The assistant gives wrong answers" is not a cost problem, and the Overview tab will never show it. The **Feedback** tab will — on plans that carry it. **Feedback** and **Terminations** are Enterprise tabs; without that licence Usage & Monitoring shows **Overview** only, and a deep link to one of the other two lands on Overview.

It lists the thumbs up and down your users left on AI answers, with the cards **Positive**, **Negative**, **With Comments** and **With Conversation**, and a **Positive rate** percentage. An amber banner appears when the positive share falls below **60%** on a sample of at least **5** items.

HR at Van Dijk Groep sits at 48%. Filtering to the Negative chip and reading the comments shows eight complaints pointing at one outdated policy in a knowledge base — and an entry carries a model or tier badge whenever the model behind the answer is known, so you can see whether one model is responsible.

steps.question: Marieke opens Usage & Monitoring on a colleague's screen and sees only the Overview tab — no Feedback, no Terminations. What is going on?

choices.label: Those two tabs come with the Enterprise licence for advanced usage monitoring. Overview is what every organisation admin gets.
Her colleague lacks the organisation-admin role, so the page renders in a reduced form.
choices.feedback: Without the organisation-admin role the whole Settings → Organisation group is out of reach — there would be no Usage & Monitoring page at all, not a page with fewer tabs.

choices.label: The two tabs only appear once the organisation is over 80% of its cost cap.
choices.feedback: The cap gauge and the tab row are unrelated. Feedback and Terminations are there from day one on a plan that includes them, whether the gauge reads 4% or 96%.

choices.label: The RANGE control is set to Today, and there is nothing to show in either tab yet.
choices.feedback: An empty tab still renders — you would read No feedback entries or No terminations match the filters. And the range control is hidden while those tabs are open anyway.

steps.explanation: Gates come in two kinds and they stack: a role decides whether you may see the Organisation settings at all, and the licence decides how much of a screen you get. Here the role is fine and the plan is the limit, so the quality half of this lesson is simply not on that workspace — the cost half on Overview still is.

steps.title: Terminations: tasks that stopped early
steps.bodyMd:
The **Terminations** tab is the other quality screen: *tasks that ended early — token limits, errors, or aborts*. Its cards are **Total**, **Max tokens**, **Max iterations**, **Errors**, **Aborted** (client disconnects) and **Large input**.

Read the four types as four different diagnoses:

- **Max tokens** — the answer ran out of room. Usually a long input or a long expected output.
- **Max iterations** — an agent looped through tool calls without converging.
- **Error** — the provider or a tool failed; the row carries an error code.
- **Aborted** — the user closed the tab or navigated away.

Messages are never logged here; only sanitised metadata is shown.

steps.question: Pieter's procurement routine at Van Dijk Groep dies halfway through its supplier PDFs, most days. Which tab explains why?

choices.label: Terminations — it records why a task stopped early, and its By agent chart points at the offender.
Feedback — a failed routine shows up there as a negative rating.
choices.feedback: Feedback only holds ratings a person deliberately left on an answer. A routine running overnight has nobody there to press a thumb.

choices.label: Overview — the By app area panel shows the failure rate per part of the product.
choices.feedback: Overview counts calls and spend, not outcomes. A run that stopped halfway still logged its calls and looks perfectly normal there.

choices.label: None of them — the routine's own run history is the only place a stop is recorded.
choices.feedback: The run history tells you that it stopped; Terminations tells you the kind of stop, on which model, after how many iterations, and with which error code — which is what you need to fix it.

steps.explanation: Terminations is the organisation-wide view of early stops. Filter the type to Max tokens, or type the routine's name into Search agent / model / error...; the row itself carries the iteration count and the duration, and opening it adds the error class and the attachment size.

steps.question: Sales proposals come back cut off. Terminations shows Max tokens dominating, most rows carrying a Large input badge. Which TWO moves address that?

choices.label: Split the RFP upload or trim the context the step sends, so the prompt stops crowding out the answer.
Move that step to a tier with more room for the answer.
Raise the cost cap on License & Usage.
choices.feedback: The cap is a monthly money ceiling. It has no effect on how long a single answer may be — a truncated proposal would come back just as truncated on a higher cap.

choices.label: Switch AI usage sharing off so sales gets its own slice.
choices.feedback: That divides the budget differently; it changes who runs out of money first, not how much room one answer has. The proposals would still be cut off.

steps.explanation: Max tokens plus Large input is a size problem inside one call, so both fixes work on that call: send less in, or allow more out. Budget settings live on a different axis entirely — they decide who may spend, not how long an answer may be.

steps.title: Your turn: write the note to the heaviest user
steps.instruction: You are Marieke, the organisation admin at Van Dijk Groep. The gauge is at 86% with eleven days left in the billing period. Top users by cost shows Sanne in sales at roughly a third of the total, By tier shows nearly all of it on a Deep Thinking tier, and By app area points at the proposal routine. Write the short message you would send Sanne (4-6 sentences). A strong note names what you saw and where you saw it, says plainly what happens at 100% and who it hits, proposes one concrete change to the routine rather than a vague 'use it less', and offers the per-user split as the fallback if nothing changes. Keep the tone collegial: she is doing her job, the routine is the problem.
steps.placeholder: e.g. Hi Sanne — quick heads-up on our AI budget. We're at 86% of this period's cap with eleven days to go, and the usage report shows the proposal routine...

steps.title: What you can do now
steps.bodyMd:
- **Read before you turn a knob.** The cost · 30d amount on a member row names the heaviest user before you open anything; the gauge then tells you how deep into the billing period you are, and Top users by cost, By tier and By app area turn a percentage into a person, a tier and a part of the product.
- **Know which control does what.** The cap is money and lives on License & Usage. AI usage sharing splits that same cap per seat — it is fairness, not savings — and both are reversible.
- **Separate cost from quality.** Feedback answers "are the answers any good", Terminations answers "why did it stop". Neither question is answered by the spend chart.

ex-usage-caps-note.title: A note that turns a percentage into a decision
ex-usage-caps-note.task: Write a short collegial message from Marieke, the organisation admin, to Sanne in sales — the heaviest AI user at Van Dijk Groep — after the cap gauge hit 86% with eleven days left in the billing period, the usage report attributed about a third of the spend to her, almost all of it on a Deep Thinking tier, from the proposal routine.
criteria: Names the evidence and where it came from: the cap gauge percentage plus at least one of Top users by cost, By tier or By app area — not a vague 'you are using a lot'.
States the consequence correctly: at 100% of the cap AI calls are blocked until the next billing period, and in pooled mode that hits the whole team, not just her.
Proposes one concrete, specific change to the routine — for example moving that step off the Deep Thinking tier, or sending less input per proposal — rather than 'use it less'.
Mentions the per-user split (AI usage sharing on License & Usage) as a fallback, and frames it as splitting the same cap rather than as a punishment or a saving.
Stays collegial and factual: the routine's configuration is the problem, not the person's work.
ex-usage-caps-note.guidance: Do not pass a note that only says 'please cut back' with no evidence and no proposed change. Do not pass a note claiming the per-user split lowers the bill, that the cap controls answer length, or that usage was inspected in a place that does not exist (there is no export or download on this report). Do not pass a note that threatens to remove her access, or that reports token or call counts — a cloud organisation admin never sees those. Partial credit is fine when the tone and the evidence are right but the fallback is missing.

practiceTopic.title: Caps, spikes and quality signals
practiceTopic.summary: How an organisation admin reads the cap gauge, decides between a pooled and a per-user budget, and uses the Feedback and Terminations tabs.
facts: The cap warning email is sent once per billing period to at most five administrator addresses; at 100% of the cost cap AI calls are blocked until the next period, while the reporting screens keep working.
The bar AI usage vs. cap is green below 80%, amber from 80% and red from 95%, and it measures the billing period, which follows the subscription's billing cycle start rather than the calendar month.
The RANGE presets are Today, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, All and Custom, with 30d selected on open; the range moves the lists under the gauge but never the gauge itself.
The cost cap and the section AI usage sharing, with the toggle Share AI usage across the organisation, live on Settings → Organisation → License & Usage, not on Usage & Monitoring.
With sharing off each active seat gets the cap divided by the number of active seats, while the organisation-wide 80% warning still fires off the pooled total, so the bill itself does not go down.

The Feedback tab (Enterprise licence, like Terminations) shows Positive, Negative, With Comments and With Conversation with a Positive rate, and warns below 60% positive on at least 5 items; without that licence only Overview renders.
The Terminations tab groups early stops as Max tokens, Max iterations, Errors and Aborted, adds a Large input signal, and logs only sanitised metadata — never message content.

Users & Groups shows an AI amount captioned cost · 30d on each member row, tooltip {calls} requests · {cost} (last 30 days); it is a rolling 30 days rather than the billing period, and only members with recorded spend get one.
